newsitem.title: GERMANY: Union criticises Kohl government on jobs policies.
newsitem.headline: Union criticises Kohl government on jobs policies.

text.p: Germany's DAG white-collar union at the weekend accused Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition government of doing too little to help reduce the nation's record unemployment rate.

Union chief Roland Issen said, "An additional 100,000 unemployed workers will be the ones bearing the brunt of the five billion marks in cuts in the Labour Office's budget, which are at the government's disposal."

In light of record unemployment rates, an aggressive government policy would be needed next year to combat the problem, Issen said. "The government must finally realise that it is more sensible to pay for jobs than to pay unemployment insurance."
Issen was particularly critical of the government's efforts to retrain workers, saying the Kohl government was not going far enough.

While several politicians have said Germany's jobless rate, perched at a post-unification record of 4.1 million in November, may be on the verge of improving next year, they also said the situation could get worse before it gets better.

"I see an impending change in the situation on the German labour market," Wolfgang Schaeuble, the powerful parliamentary leader for Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats told German paper Bild am Sonntag.
But he added that rough winter weather conditions could force the jobless rate to climb more next year.
Schaeuble however stuck by his party's goal to halve Germany's jobless rate by the year 2000 and urged companies to create more jobs.
He welcomed signs that German companies were starting to rethink strategies that make their immediate obligation boosting profits and pleasing shareholders.
